tasks.task: Write the positioning and one-page message sheet

items.when: When buyer evidence is gathered and you need the position, proof and words on one page
Before you commit, to see several ways to stand apart, each with its own position
When the position will not fit in one sentence, to draft and compare short versions
When everyone in the market sounds alike and the message must be one rivals cannot copy
When the main claim is drafted, to test it is specific, true and not already a rival's
When the position starts from features, to start again from what buyers would use instead

tasks.task: Turn reviews, calls and lost deals into buyer evidence

items.when: At the start of positioning work, to turn raw material into alternatives, values and words
When you have interviews, surveys or tickets and need patterns and buyers' own words
When there is too little evidence, to interview five to eight recent buyers on why they bought
When interview notes are in, to map each buying story and the forces behind the switch
When you have notes on won and lost deals, to find why you really win
When the evidence is a list of feature requests, to ask what job the buyer hired this for

tasks.task: Build a buyer profile and pick the first audience

items.when: When you have orders and reviews and need a job-based profile writers can use
When you need the customer's job written down and the real rivals for that job named
When there are several possible audiences, to compare them and pick one to start with

tasks.task: Map what rivals claim and find the open gap

items.when: When you need a dated table of what five or more rivals and alternatives claim
When you have rival links and need site, pricing and positioning for each
When you want the word each rival owns in buyers' minds and the words nobody owns
When the gap is found, to draft messages that claim it
When the client wants to claim a place a bigger rival already holds

tasks.task: Run the quarterly positioning and rival review

items.when: Every quarter, or when a major rival launches, prices move or win rates change
Between reviews, to keep a monthly record of what each rival changed
When closed deals are logged, to see loss stages, common objections and who you lose to
When the review jumps to new tactics, to go back to the market and the chosen buyer first

tasks.task: Publish a fair comparison or alternatives page

items.when: When the client wants a 'vs' page, an alternatives page or a table that names rivals
When you need a like-for-like comparison where every line can be verified and dated
Before writing, to choose between best-of, review, alternative and versus pages
When one rival is named and you need a fair page built to rank and persuade
When the table itself must help people choose, not only list ticks
Before publishing, to see which claims are supported and which go too far

tasks.task: Check every claim in a page, ad or sales sheet

items.when: When copy makes objective or comparative claims that a rival or regulator could test
When you have the copy and the evidence, to match each claim to its support
When an ad is the piece under review, to pair every claim with proof and list the gaps

tasks.task: Check the homepage against the message sheet

items.when: After the message sheet is agreed, to check the page line by line and rewrite weak lines
When the top of the page fails, to get five headlines with a subhead and a pick
When you want to see what a named buyer thinks at each scroll of the page
When a new headline is drafted, to check it picks the right reader and promises a gain

tasks.task: Review or draft the pricing page and packaging

items.when: When the pricing page confuses buyers or the plans no longer fit how people buy
When the plans are undecided, to draft a three-step ladder and see how it reads
When the value metric and tiers are in doubt and need a reasoned proposal and test plan
When nobody knows what buyers would pay, to ask customers two questions and read the range
When the plan table is drafted, to check it helps a buyer choose between plans

tasks.task: Plan a product or feature launch

items.when: When a product, feature or relaunch has a target date and needs the whole run in order
When a small team needs the plan from an optional demand test to the review two weeks after
When the date is fixed and the plan is too big, to see a half-scope version
A few days before launch, to get a clear go or no-go with the blockers listed
When the plan is heavy for a small team, to cut it to what a solo maker would ship

tasks.task: Design a cheap demand test before building or launching

items.when: Before building or launching, when it is unclear whether buyers will act
When you want several cheap test types to compare, such as a page or a pre-order
When the best test is to sell it to three real buyers before it exists
Before spending on the test, to get a blunt review of what is weak in the idea

tasks.task: Write every launch message in one voice

items.when: Once the launch plan and message sheet exist, to write email, posts, page and partner notes
When the launch runs on an email list and needs a full sequence with a close date
When the announcement needs posts made for each social platform
When the launch line is correct but dull, to get a simpler, more concrete version
When the pack is drafted, to list the hard questions it raises and answer them

tasks.task: Brief sales and support before the launch

items.when: A few working days before launch, to give sales and support one page plus objections
When sales face one named rival and need comparisons and reply scripts
When the team needs a one-pager, an objection sheet or a deck outline for the launch
When an objection has no good answer yet, to work out what it means and how to reply

tasks.task: Plan a beta and decide when it is ready to open up

items.when: When you need who to invite, what to ask them and clear rules for ending the beta
When a feature ships through a beta with measures set before it starts

tasks.task: Review the launch and report what was learned

items.when: Two weeks after launch, to compare results with the targets the plan set
When a software launch needs a decision on what to keep, fix or stop
When you have launch numbers and need trends, wins, misses and what to change

tasks.task: Announce a feature or update to existing customers

items.when: When changes need writing up as release notes or a roadmap story for customers
When the same value must be said differently for marketing, sales and onboarding
When the announcement says 'powerful' and 'seamless', to make each line true and specific

tasks.task: Write the value proposition and selling points

items.when: When you have the offer and customer facts and need the gain stated in one place
When features must become selling points in the order buyers care about
When the value could be framed several ways and you want to compare them
When the proposition is drafted, to test whether a rival could say the same thing

tasks.task: Name a product or feature and test its tagline

items.when: When a launch or rename needs name ideas, each with the reason it fits
Before naming, to see which words rivals own and which are free
When a tagline is flat, to get three versions people will remember
When a tagline is chosen, to score it against ten tests and get sharper versions

tasks.task: Gather case studies and place proof where buyers doubt

items.when: When one customer interview should become a case study and you need the evidence gaps
When you know the buyer's doubts and must choose which quote or number answers each
Each month, to check approved quotes and link every claim to its evidence

tasks.task: Choose the market, segment and route for a new product

items.when: When the product could serve many groups and needs one starting segment and a plan
When you need positioning, a route to market and launch steps in one plan
When the plan quotes a market size, to rebuild it bottom-up and mark the guesses

tasks.task: Run a win and loss review

items.when: When closed deals are logged, to find patterns in why you win and lose
When you need interviews with recent buyers and their stories mapped
When you only have rough deal notes, to pull out the real reasons and a message
When the deal notes are thin, to interview recent buyers and lost prospects on a timeline

tasks.task: Build the launch deck or product overview deck

items.when: Before slides, to outline a story that builds belief for this audience
When the outline is agreed and you want a first deck draft to edit
When the deck is outlined, to check the audience hears the stakes early

always.when: At the start, to put product facts in one file every later step reads
When copy states a number or a fact about a rival that you cannot trace to a source
Before a sheet or page is shared, to catch typos and product names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When there is too little buyer evidence and interviews or a survey must be run
When the job is the price itself, not how the pricing page explains it
When the homepage or launch page needs full new copy, not a line-by-line check
When sales need full battlecards, a deck and training beyond the one-page brief
When the launch needs a press release and pitches to reporters
When the launch emails must be built, segmented and sent, not only written

gaps: No library item checks a homepage line by line against an agreed message sheet; only the kit prompt does
No library item runs a post-launch review for a marketing launch: results against targets, what to repeat and what to drop
No library item writes a one-page launch brief for sales and support; battlecards and collateral exist but not the handoff page
No library item reads the result of a demand test against a bar set before it ran
No library item tests a message with real buyers, such as a five-second test or a message survey, and scores the answers
No library item sizes a launch into tiers so a small update does not get a full launch
No library item builds a dated, sourced feature comparison from rivals' public pages; only the kit skill does
No library item writes an hour-by-hour run sheet for launch day
No library item plans a launch on product directories or community sites step by step
